text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like KWEB on 2026-09-18, the median 10-session forward return was 0.68%, but the distribution is wide and heavily right-skewed. The single number to anchor on for path risk is the median max adverse excursion of -3.3%, which describes the typical worst drawdown a holder experienced before the horizon closed. This is a description of a historical conditional distribution, not a forecast of what KWEB will do next.

[state]
The retrieval engine selected these 50 analogs because the current state of KWEB is defined by three distinctive features. First, the distance from the 52-week high (dist52) is -42.74%, carrying a z-score of -1.899, meaning the ETF is deeply off its highs in a way that rarely occurs. Second, the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) is -2.663, with a clipped z-score of -1.607 used for matching, indicating severely depressed liquidity relative to its own history. Third, WTI crude change over 20 days (oilChg20) is 19.24% (z-score 1.124), an unusually sharp energy move. These features, weighted at 30% for name-specific price/volume traits, 20% for market context, 20% for macro, 10% for crypto, and 20% for event timing, pulled in sessions dominated by Technology (14 analogs), China ADR (7), Health Care (7), and Consumer Disc. (6).

[history]
Over the 10-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a mean return of 1.81% and a median of 0.68%, with a standard deviation of 8.19%. The distribution is highly asymmetric, with a skew of 2.601. The 10th percentile outcome was -5.81% and the 90th percentile was 8.66%. In 56% of the episodes the return was above zero, and in 44% it was below. The bad tail is populated by recent weakness: NKE on 2026-09-03 returned -8.41%, PDD on 2026-08-31 returned -7.05%, NKE on 2026-08-13 returned -6.77%, HD on 2026-09-03 returned -5.69%, and KWEB itself on 2026-08-31 returned -5.15%. The extreme positive tail is entirely driven by a single outlier: NIO on 2025-07-08 returned 43.14%. Without that single episode, the upper tail collapses.

[tails]
A position can finish near flat and still be un-holdable through the path. Across the 50 analogs, the median max adverse excursion was -3.3%. The 25th percentile of max adverse excursion was -5.96%, and the 10th percentile was -7.26%. Looking at breach probabilities, 32% of the analog paths breached a 5% drawdown at some point during the 10 sessions. Only 2% breached a 10% drawdown, and 0% breached 15% or 20%. The median max favourable excursion was 4.04%, yielding a reward-risk ratio of 1.22.

[stress]
The baseline median across all 50 analogs is 0.68%. Several stress scenarios materially worsen this picture. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario produced a median forward return of -9.75% across 48 analogs, a delta of -10.43% versus baseline, with a 75% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns, making it a sample of one regime, not a forecast. The 2025-04 tariff shock scenario yielded a median of -3.36% across 26 analogs, a delta of -4.04%, with a 65.4% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail of the distribution asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The 2022 inflation/rate bear scenario showed a median of -4.81% across 50 analogs, a delta of -5.49%, with a 30% breach probability; caveat: a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind produced a median of -2.77% across 36 analogs, a delta of -3.45%; caveat: reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare had a median of -3.08% across 50 analogs, a delta of -3.76%; caveat: ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters late-window analogs. Milder shocks included earnings release day (median -1.25%, delta -1.93%, caveat: 6-K dates are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02), liquidity air pocket (median -0.51%, delta -1.19%, caveat: gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, bounding reference-market gap risk only), rates-up (median -0.41%, delta -1.09%, caveat: uses DGS3MO/T10Y2Y levels as proxies), vol-spike (median 0.67%, delta -0.01%, caveat: VIX shocks mean-revert quickly), weekend-hold-7x24 (median 0.52%, delta -0.16%, caveat: blocks are paired by index modulo block count, a deterministic convention, not a joint distribution), china-adr-shock (median 0.49%, delta -0.19%, caveat: delisting risks are structural and will not appear in a price/vol feature space), crypto-contagion (median 0.78%, delta 0.1, caveat: BTC feature is a market-wide proxy, fng excluded from distance), fomc-day (median 0.2, delta -0.48, caveat: only 92 decision days exist, so the set is small and overlapping), and 2023-03 regional bank stress (median 4.4, delta 3.72, caveat: very short window dominated by a handful of sessions). No scenarios were skipped.

[reasoning]
The three most relevant scenarios for this idea are the 2025-04 tariff shock, because it directly targets China-linked cash flows and produced a 65.4% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown across 26 analogs with a -4.04% delta versus baseline; the 2020-02/03 liquidity crash, because the current dv20z of -2.663 makes liquidity regimes highly relevant, and it produced the worst median (-9.75%) and highest breach rate (75%) across 48 analogs; and the 2022 inflation/rate bear, because it isolates multiple compression without an earnings collapse across 50 analogs with a -5.49% delta. A reader should distrust the heavy concentration of 2025 (23 analogs) and 2026 (15 analogs) in the retrieval set, which means the distribution is overwhelmingly shaped by the last two years rather than a broad historical base. No scenario contradicts the direction of the baseline distribution, as the baseline itself is only slightly positive at 0.68%.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The honest verdict from the engine's validation is: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." Out-of-sample conformal coverage was 83.6% against an 80% target, but the matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name unconditional benchmark was -2.4%, meaning the naive benchmark is tighter. For path risk, the engine targets a 10% drawdown level. The mean predicted breach rate across 2627 test queries was 8.7%, while the realised breach rate was 5.6%. The calibration gap is 3.15 percentage points with a clustered standard error of 1.12, meaning the model systematically overstates how often the path breaches. The Brier score for the analog share was 0.0534, compared to 0.0591 for the volatility reflection benchmark, 0.0587 for the same-name calibration, and 0.0576 for the pooled calibration. The paired Brier difference versus the volatility reflection benchmark has a 95% confidence interval of [-0.0115, 0.0004], which spans zero and is therefore unresolved. The differences versus same-name calibration (interval [-0.0097, -0.0012]) and pooled calibration (interval [-0.008, -0.0006]) do not span zero and are resolved in favor of the analog. Regarding the wrapper, the status is "measured" on Bitget official MCP (agent.bitget.com/mcp) for the KWEB/USDT RWA perpetual futures trading 24/7. The reference market is shut for 75.98% of the week, and 68.49% of the wrapper's own hourly movement landed in those closed hours. The tracking tier is "tight tracker" with a return correlation of 0.9813 and a tracking error of 32 bp/day. The basis band is -0.13% to 0.51%, and the spread is 24.19 bps. Caveat: a tight perpetual is not the underlying and not a redeemable spot token; funding applies, and the basis means the exit price differs from the reference close the analog distribution is built on. The return layer measured 6 distinct weekend blocks. The median weekend block return was 0.1215%, the 10th percentile was -0.976%, and the standard deviation was 0.9046%. The median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.331%, and 0% of weekends breached the 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions.
